### SessionStore

Interface. `import type { SessionStore } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime/session";`

```ts
export interface SessionStore {
    get(id: string): StoredSession | undefined | null | Promise<StoredSession | undefined | null>;
    set(id: string, data: StoredSession, ttlSeconds: number): void | Promise<void>;
    delete(id: string): void | Promise<void>;
}
```

Where store-mode sessions keep their data. The cookie then holds only a random, signed id.
`ttlSeconds` is how long the record must live; drop it after that (the session also checks its
own expiry, so a store that ignores the TTL only keeps dead records around).

Members:

- `get`: The record of `id`, or undefined / null when there is none.
- `set`: Stores the record of `id`, to keep for `ttlSeconds`.
- `delete`: Removes the record of `id`.

Uses: [`StoredSession`](#storedsession).

Used by: [`SessionOptions`](#sessionoptions), [`SessionConfig`](#sessionconfig).

### SessionOptions

Interface. `import type { SessionOptions } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime/session";`

```ts
export interface SessionOptions {
    cookieName?: string;
    maxAge?: number;
    rolling?: boolean;
    store?: SessionStore;
}
```

The options of [`defineSession`](#definesession).

Members:

- `cookieName`: Cookie name. Default `"nowaki_session"`.
- `maxAge`: Lifetime in seconds. Default 7 days.
- `rolling`: `true` (default): each write, and a read past half the lifetime, extends the session by
  `maxAge`. `false`: the session ends `maxAge` after sign-in (`regenerate()`) or creation.
- `store`: Keeps the data server-side instead of in the encrypted cookie (which is limited to 4 KB).

Uses: [`SessionStore`](#sessionstore).

Used by: [`SessionConfig`](#sessionconfig), [`defineSession`](#definesession).

### defineSession

Function. `import { defineSession } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime/session";`

```ts
export function defineSession(options?: SessionOptions): SessionConfig;
```

Session options, in the app root's `session.ts`. Without the file, `ctx.session` uses the
defaults. The cookie is encrypted (or, with a store, signed) with keys derived from
`NOWAKI_SESSION_SECRET`; production refuses to use a session without it. Throws on an unknown
option or an invalid value.

Example:

```tsx
// session.ts
import { defineSession } from "@nowaki-dev/runtime/session";
export default defineSession({ maxAge: 60 * 60 * 24 * 30 });
```

Uses: [`SessionOptions`](#sessionoptions), [`SessionConfig`](#sessionconfig).
